You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Gramercy Property Trust / BRE Glacier realized record after going-private acquisition, ~3-5-year horizon

> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; this sub-dossier documents the
> reporting-status facts and what could and could not be independently traced. It
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- Gramercy Property Trust's last periodic annual report on EDGAR (CIK 1297587) is a
  Form 10-K for fiscal year 2017, filed 2018-03-01; no Form 10-K or 20-F was filed under
  this CIK at any later date. [SRC: SEC EDGAR submissions listing for CIK 1297587, accessed via https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001297587.json]
- On October 22, 2018, BRE Glacier L.P. (as successor by merger to Gramercy Property
  Trust) filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of registration of the common and
  Series A preferred shares, reporting zero holders of record for each class as of the
  certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063186, Form 15-12B]
- GPT Operating Partnership LP (CIK 1708204), the operating-partnership tier, likewise
  has no Form 10-K filed after the 2018-03-01 fiscal-2017 report and filed a Form
  15-15D on the same date, October 22, 2018, terminating its own reporting obligations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063187, Form 15-15D]
- A search of the EDGAR company-name index for "BRE Glacier" (the surviving legal
  entity) returns no registrant record, i.e., no separate SEC filer/CIK exists for the
  successor entity. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=BRE+Glacier&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&output=atom]
- Consequently, no audited public financial statements or periodic disclosures exist for
  this business, under either its former or successor name, for the years following the
  October 2018 closing, including the approximate 2021-2023 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063186, Form 15-12B]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063187, Form 15-15D]

## Acquirer-level disclosure search
- The acquiring Parent entity was described at signing as an affiliate of Blackstone
  Real Estate Partners VIII L.P., a private real estate investment fund; no source
  retrieved for this dossier identifies a public SEC registrant (10-K/20-F filer) that
  separately discloses the operating or financial results of the specific real estate
  portfolio and asset-management business formerly held by Gramercy Property Trust. [UNVERIFIED]
- Reputable trade press reports that, in June 2023, Prologis agreed to acquire an
  approximately 14-million-square-foot industrial property portfolio from Blackstone's
  opportunistic real estate funds for $3.1 billion, spanning markets including Dallas,
  South Florida, and the New York City metro area; these reports describe the assets as
  held by Blackstone's opportunistic funds generally and do not identify them as, or
  trace them specifically to, the portfolio acquired from Gramercy Property Trust in
  2018. Any inference linking this 2023 transaction to the Gramercy portfolio
  specifically is [UNVERIFIED]. [SRC: https://www.blackstone.com/news/press/prologis-to-acquire-14msf-blackstone-industrial-portfolio-in-3-1-billion-deal/]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the acquired entity was taken private, both the parent registrant and its
  operating partnership formally terminated their SEC reporting obligations in October
  2018, and no successor registrant has since been identified, there is no traceable
  public 3-5-year outcome record for this business. The reporting-status facts above are
  stated plainly; no outcome scalar (financial performance, impairment, disposition, or
  otherwise) can be sourced to a public primary filing for this entity, and none is
  asserted. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063186, Form 15-12B]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-063187, Form 15-15D]

[SLICE END]
